about: Oops! All Berries is the front of a Cap'n Crunch cereal box with the mascot's portrait cut out, leaving an empty white circle at the top where the Cap'n would normally wave at you. Below it the logo reads "Oops! All" over a blue banner, and a bowl overflows with red, blue, green and purple berry balls. The real cereal's joke was a factory "mistake" that left only the best part in the box. The meme turns that into a label for anything that turns out to be one single ingredient, usually the worst one.
origin: Quaker Oats introduced Cap'n Crunch's Oops! All Berries in 1997, pitched as a happy production accident. Photoshopped parody boxes of the cereal circulated online for years before this blank cutout became a template.
usage:
The first box sits in the empty circle: put a face, a name or a short label for who made the "mistake". The second box is on the blue banner under "Oops! All" and finishes the product name, so write the one thing the box is full of.

It is perfect for anything that is 100 percent one thing: a playlist that is all sad songs, a codebase that is all bugs, a team that is all goalkeepers, a group chat that is all memes. Plural nouns read best on the banner.
